label: Successive supplier lists can favor an endless chain over a fixed mixture of finite depths
paraphrase: Starting at recipient zero on the same natural-number roster, an audit of the first k complete lists of the endless chain matches the finite-depth world n exactly when k ≤ n. Thus every finite prefix matches both the endless relation and a sourced relation with a supplierless ancestor of zero. If the next complete list is empty at depth d, only sourced depth d matches that record within these classes. Under one fixed proper nonnegative prior on the finite depths, the matching prefix has finite-class likelihood one minus the cumulative mass below k and endless likelihood one. With fixed positive class weights, sufficiently long prefixes favor the endless class by any prescribed finite positive factor, but there is no cutoff uniform over proper priors: at each length, concentrating at that depth gives likelihood one. A full-support geometric prior gives positive likelihood (1/2)^k and rules out preference by every factor at any one finite k.
